feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, relevant progression, and solid evidence of scope across web, content, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, tighter structure, and removal of some redundancy across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and experience consistently position you as a digital strategy and communications lead.  
- Strong credibility through progression: multiple promotions at NACo show growth, trust, and increasing responsibility.  
- Good specificity: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, studio buildout, and 10,000+ page migration add substance and technical depth.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve scannability and save space.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: use “12 years of experience” (missing “of”); standardize serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “cross-channel” and “organization-wide” are consistent, but date style (“Oct.”/“Sept.”/“Mar.”) should be uniform throughout. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding a clearer leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct punctuation.
- Lead with current positioning and strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a tighter formulation such as “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading multi-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, Drupal-based platform improvement, and building the workflows, governance, and systems that support complex teams. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap heavily with Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” is reinforced throughout NACo roles, so keep it brief here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if it emphasized higher-value leadership capabilities over tool-adjacent or repetitive phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and elevate wording: use “Digital transformation leadership” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” and “Cross-channel communications” instead of “Multi-channel communication.”
- Prioritize strategic, recent strengths: digital transformation, editorial systems/governance, CMS/platform modernization, analytics/insights, advocacy communications, and multimedia/event production.
- Make phrasing parallel and concise; avoid mixing broad functions (“strategy”) with narrower tasks (“Web & CMS administration”).
- Possible rewrite: Digital transformation leadership • Cross-channel communications • CMS and web platform management • Editorial systems and governance • Analytics, reporting and optimization • Workflow and systems design • Stakeholder and cross-functional coordination • Policy and advocacy communications • Multimedia and live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Data analytics & reporting” repeat detail covered more specifically in Topline Skills and Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and “Recent Projects.” Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes or scale where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into impact-focused lines, e.g.:
- “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Improved enterprise web operations by refining workflows, analytics, governance, and cross-channel publishing practices across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaigns launched, workflow time saved, search accuracy gains, or engagement improvements.
- Reduce generic phrasing like “support,” “advise,” and “deliver”; use stronger verbs such as led, built, streamlined, launched, improved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating project-level detail already listed in “Recent Projects” unless you add outcomes here.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” also echoes the header and NACo role; keep this version specific to current consulting impact.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, budget, and multi-channel operations across web, email, social, and video.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen vague bullets with business impact: add metrics for email/social growth, video output, production savings, reporting adoption, or efficiency gains from governance/planning systems.
- Condense tool list in the analytics bullet: “Built a cross-platform analytics stack and executive reporting system using GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Clarity.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with older multimedia bullets unless framed as a new capability at organizational scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid mid-level progression entry, but it overlaps heavily with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and specific to what you owned before stepping into broader strategy/platform leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging for county-official audiences.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points: newsletter management, launch/growth of weekly advocacy video, cross-team editorial calendar/processes, publishing workflow improvements.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter sends/open rates, video cadence/views, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated, publishing volume, turnaround-time improvements.
- Example phrasing: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders” and “Built a recurring weekly advocacy video update into an established policy communications channel.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” risk repeating governance/operations language already used in the Director role.
- Video/livestream language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling a recurring program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and work experience. It should be tighter and more distinctive, emphasizing strategic leadership rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector digital communications
- Audience and journey-based content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “digital communications” to sound more senior and operationally aligned with the CV.
- If space allows, make one skill more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Content governance for high-volume, multi-publisher environments.”
- Keep this section at the capability level; save advocacy/campaign specifics for recent roles and projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is also repeated elsewhere; avoid restating both terms unless this section is trimmed elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. In Topline Skills, this should signal current strengths and outcomes-oriented capabilities, not repeat the full stack list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software inventory to capability-led phrasing tied to recent work.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here: remove jQuery unless required by target roles.
- If SharePoint/Power Pages matter for the target job, keep one concise mention; otherwise leave them to Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages are already listed in Technical + IT, so avoid repeating the same exhaustive platform list here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-level capability and decision impact rather than repeat platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to strategic capability: “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting”
- Keep only the most relevant platforms and group them: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity”
- Tighten the final phrase to outcomes-oriented language: replace “SEO and performance analysis” with “SEO, UX and conversion/performance optimization”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive reporting dashboards • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool stack.
- “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive reporting” and overlaps with “analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear but too generic as a standalone skills item, and it overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this line should signal depth or be trimmed to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider emphasizing level: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views)” to connect the skill to recent achievement.
- Keep platform names only; avoid mixing in modernization or implementation terms here since those already appear elsewhere.
- If this section is meant to be more technical, consider replacing “GitHub Pages” with a stronger enterprise-relevant platform only if applicable.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates Topline Skills [2]; consider deleting one or making this version platform-only and the other execution-focused.
- Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint are already reinforced in recent experience, so don’t over-explain them here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Tag management • Edge/serverless scripting • CI/CD
- Replace older/version-specific terms with cleaner phrasing: use HTML/CSS instead of HTML5/CSS3; keep JavaScript, move jQuery last or drop if not current.
- Clarify tools by function: Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD) to show practical application, not just names.
- If accurate, add scope via parenthetical context: “API integrations (CMS, analytics, campaign tools)” or “Cloudflare Workers (edge logic/prototyping).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills item “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations • Workflow automation”; avoid repeating the same sequence verbatim.
- GTM may also fit under analytics/optimization if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to grouped capability language: “Workflow automation & collaboration: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project/issue management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; team operations: Slack, Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant automation tools first and de-emphasize basic collaboration tools.
- If space allows, add light context tied to recent work: “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Team Operations” to better match senior-level positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating them verbatim in multiple sections.
- Slack/Teams may be too basic to merit space unless grouped as collaboration tools rather than featured skills.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare to add much value on its own. It should be tightened and framed to support the stronger email/communications evidence already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency and standardize naming: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope in brief parentheticals: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member email/community) • Mailchimp (newsletter distribution)
- If these platforms were central in recent roles, consider adding one measurable qualifier elsewhere instead of here, e.g., “managed newsletter platforms reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets already covering email newsletters and digital channel leadership; avoid repeating audience-size claims in this skills line.
- “Engagement” may feel vague unless paired with a clearer function like “member engagement” or “email automation.”

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete scope or outputs if you have them.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add specific contributions and scale where possible: website refresh, number of livestreams/videos produced, cadence of weekly updates, audience/event reach, or process improvements.
- Tighten the management point: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised one digital media associate,” if accurate.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, support a major website refresh, and establish cross-channel production workflows. Produced livestreams and weekly video updates for advocacy and member communications, while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow language already used in later NACo roles unless you can add distinct outcomes.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened to emphasize ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific line such as: “Produced multimedia and digital content to support policy communications and organizational programs.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes launched, audiences reached, internal teams supported, or types/volume of research projects coordinated.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles since the stronger digital leadership story appears in 2015–2024 positions.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia/video language already covered in the 2015–2024 NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; position it as the foundation for later media and platform leadership.
